method: One procedure, fitted on the public training pages only, written as a whole book and sent with cut book: 4,500 ordinary lines and 740 paragraph-opening lines, laid onto every page of the manuscript in order. (1) A glyph chain over the whole line, with the word space and the line end as ordinary symbols; each glyph is drawn given the four symbols before it, or, 6 times in 10, given only the two before it; it starts afresh at each line, from one start mark for a line that opens a paragraph and another for any other line. (2) Three tables, fitted on the public pages labelled Currier A, Currier B and unlabelled. At each point of the book the writer uses the table of the public page that lies at that point (by share of lines written), as a scribe would whose exemplar or habit changes from sheet to sheet. (3) Each table keeps its own memory. At the start of any word but the first of a line: with probability 0.20 the writer takes one of the last 15 words written under that table (on a paragraph-opening line, only words already on that line) and changes one glyph to another that the chain allows between its neighbours; with probability 0.45 (ordinary lines only) it writes again, whole, a word standing at least twice among the last 300 words written under that table. In both cases it prefers a word whose first glyph the chain allows after what was just written. No rule names a glyph or a word; the only labels used are those of public pages. Lines holding a four-word run of the manuscript are redrawn. Fairness: the procedure cannot know a hidden page's language; on the practice split the public page lying at the same point of the book has the evaluation page's label for 29 of 34 pages. Local result, practice split, three seeds, none selected: every established fact holds on 3 of 3; same-language minus different-language page similarity 0.127, 0.080, 0.110 (manuscript 0.122); labels dealt among whole pages, p at or below 0.01 on 2 of 3; labels rotated along the page order, at or below 0.05 on 0 of 3. So this text, seed 1, reproduces the level and the deal null and is expected NOT to pass the rotation: it is sent as the strongest attempt I have, to put on the record whether the fact stands against it. If it stands, it does so by the rotation null alone, which has no margin at this sample size.
